messages:
Jordan: Quick sync — running a fresh design pass on the model catalog compare flow. Main items: sticky filter chips when you enter compare, clarify performance badges (latency/cost), and tighten version-pinning microcopy. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/model-catalog
Sam: looked at the figma. two quick ideas: keep filters sticky but collapse into a condensed row when scrolling compare table; when condensed, show a single "Filters (3)" pill instead of full chips.
Maya (Product): +1 for condensed row. Concern: users may think filters are lost if compressed. Need a clear affordance to expand. Maybe a small chevron and label "filters".
Devin (Eng): sticky chips are fine, but watch reflow when table rows render — continuous batching in the runtime causes width jitter. Suggest `position: sticky; top: 72px;` and reserving the header height so the table doesn't jump.
Aria (Accessibility): keyboard focus order matters here. If we make a condensed pill that expands, it must be reachable by keyboard and announce the expanded state. Use `aria-expanded` on the pill and ensure `aria-controls` points to the filter panel.
Sam (Design): for the performance badges, proposal: shorten copy on badge — e.g. small badge reads "P99: 120ms" and tooltip shows full text: "P99 latency (24h, us-east-1): 120ms — measured across production traffic".
Jordan: sounds good. Can we also show cost per M tokens as a secondary line in the tooltip? Product wants unit economics visible in-place.
Devin (Eng): tooltip ok. Rendering per-row tooltips at scale may increase DOM nodes; we can lazy-render tooltip content on hover/focus. Also prefer a single accessible tooltip component.
Maya (Product): microcopy for pinning: current is "Pin version" which feels generic. Suggest: primary action label = "Pin for compare" and secondary tiny hint under version = "Pinned: keeps this variant in compare views".
Sam (Design): agree. Also animate the pin toggle slightly (120ms fade + scale) to make state change obvious. But keep motion reduced for users who prefer reduced-motion.
Aria (Accessibility): animation must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For the pin toggle, use `role="button"` and `aria-pressed` to convey state to screen readers. Also ensure color isn't the only indicator — add a clear icon + textual sr-only "Pinned" label.
Devin (Eng): implementation note: pinning triggers an api call to update user preferences and then updates the compare table. We should optimistically flip the UI to reduce latency, but add a small subtle error state if the call fails: inline toast: "Couldn't pin version — try again" with retry action.
Sam (Design): copy for error toast: short: "Pin failed. Try again." CTA: "Retry"
Maya (Product): telemetry ask: add metric `pin_action_failure_rate` and surface in console alerts so PMs can detect regressions after releases.
Jordan: follow-ups: Sam to update figma with condensed filter pill + chevron. Aria to provide short a11y checklist for the panel. Devin to prototype sticky with reserved header space and optimistic pin flow. Maya to draft final copy and confirm telemetry requirements.
Sam (Design): will update figma by EOD. Attaching quick gif in thread for the condensed pill demo.
ui-bot: Deploy preview for branch `catalog/compare-sticky-filters` available at https://preview.redwood.ai/compare/fix-2043 — preview expires in 48h.
Devin (Eng): testing note — found a small jitter when table uses virtual scroll and sticky header; adding a 1px transform fix to force GPU compositing helps: `transform: translateZ(0)`.
Aria (Accessibility): quick a11y nit — when filters expand, focus should move into the first interactive filter control, not stay on the pill. That avoids keyboard users losing context.
Maya (Product): okay; timeline: try to ship in next minor (two-week) release. If any blockers, flag in #release-war-room.
Jordan: thanks all — will compile the checklist and drop a tracked task in JIRA. :sparkles:
